html: The Yuhup, written Juhup in Colombia and Yuhupdëh in Brazil, are a small forest people of the north-west Amazon, between the Vaupés, Tiquié and Apaporis rivers on the border of Brazil and Colombia. They speak a language of the Nadahup family, once called Makú, close to that of the Hupd'äh. Unlike the river-dwelling Tukanoan peoples around them, such as the Taiwano, they lived mainly as forest hunters and gatherers, moving between camps, and had long unequal ties with the river peoples, trading meat and forest goods for crops. Today most live in larger villages near missions and schools.
